agents.name: Tremelimumab
agents.explanation: Blocks a different brake, CTLA-4, on immune cells early in their response. This can strengthen their response to cancer.
agents.mechanism: Blocks a different brake, CTLA-4, on immune cells early in their response. This can strengthen their response to cancer.
visual: Blocks a different brake, CTLA-4, on immune cells early in their response. This can strengthen their response to cancer.
agents.watch: Given once on cycle 1 day 1; immune side effects can appear later.

agents.name: Durvalumab
agents.explanation: Blocks a signal called PD-L1 that some cancers use to switch off immune cells. This can help immune cells recognise and attack cancer.
agents.mechanism: Blocks a signal called PD-L1 that some cancers use to switch off immune cells. This can help immune cells recognise and attack cancer.
visual: Blocks a signal called PD-L1 that some cancers use to switch off immune cells. This can help immune cells recognise and attack cancer.
agents.watch: Immune cells can inflame healthy organs, including after the final infusion. Carry your immunotherapy alert card.

sections.title: Your first visit
sections.text: Tremelimumab is given once over about one hour. Durvalumab begins 60–120 minutes after the first infusion finishes and is given over about one hour. Allow extra time for checks.

sections.title: Later visits
sections.text: Only durvalumab is repeated, every four weeks if your team advises continuing. Tremelimumab is not repeated.

sections.title: Before leaving the unit
sections.text: Write down the next infusion, blood tests and the 24-hour oncology number. Ask which appointments change if a dose is delayed. Bring the wallet and passport to your next review.

evidence.title: Why this treatment is offered
evidence.intro: First-line immunotherapy to control advanced liver cancer and help people live longer.
evidence.population: First-line advanced or unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma
evidence.interpretation: HIMALAYA compared one dose of tremelimumab plus regular durvalumab with sorafenib. Median survival was about 16.4 months with the combination and 13.8 months with sorafenib. Median means half the group lived longer and half lived for less time.
evidence.limitations: These are results in selected trial groups. They cannot predict an individual response; ask how the findings apply to you.

teachback: Which medicines are given at your next visit, and which symptoms would make you phone today?
consent_support: Discuss the aim, alternatives including supportive care alone, possible benefit, immune effects that may be serious or permanent, possible need for steroids or long-term hormone treatment, and what matters most to the patient. Discuss that only the first visit includes tremelimumab.

support.title: Carry the official immunotherapy alert card
support.text: Keep the card with you during treatment and afterwards. Show it to an out-of-hours doctor or emergency team and tell them when you last received immunotherapy.

support.title: If you become unwell
support.text: Use the 24-hour oncology number supplied by your hospital. If the team cannot be reached, seek urgent assessment. Follow the emergency action shown on your card.

support.title: Medicines and steroids
support.text: Show the team all prescription, over-the-counter and herbal medicines. Take prescribed steroids exactly as directed and ask before changing them.

support.title: Infusion visits
support.text: Tell the nurse at once about throat tightness, rash, sudden dizziness or difficulty breathing during an infusion. Ask if you need any prescribed medicine at home.

common_effects.title: Tiredness or changes in appetite
common_effects.text: Mention ongoing symptoms. Sudden exhaustion with dizziness may need urgent assessment.

common_effects.title: Itch or rash
common_effects.text: Tell your team early so they can see the skin. Blisters or peeling need urgent assessment.

common_effects.title: Loose stools
common_effects.text: Call the team about new diarrhoea even if mild; immune inflammation can worsen quickly.

serious_effects.title: Lung inflammation (pneumonitis)
serious_effects.text: Contact oncology urgently for a new cough or breathlessness. Severe trouble breathing or chest pain needs 112 or 999.

serious_effects.title: Bowel inflammation (colitis)
serious_effects.text: Call oncology urgently for new diarrhoea, blood in stools or increasing abdominal pain.

serious_effects.title: Liver inflammation or bile drainage problems
serious_effects.text: Call urgently for yellow eyes or skin, dark urine or worsening upper abdominal pain.

serious_effects.title: Hormone problems
serious_effects.text: Unusual thirst, frequent urination, dizziness, vomiting, marked weakness or severe headache need urgent assessment. Collapse or confusion with severe illness needs emergency help.

serious_effects.title: Skin, muscles or heart
serious_effects.text: Call urgently for blistering rash, new weakness, chest discomfort or palpitations. Severe chest pain, collapse or trouble breathing needs 112 or 999.

first.title: First infusion visit
first.text: Tremelimumab is given once. Durvalumab follows 60–120 minutes after the first infusion ends. Tell your nurse immediately about wheeze, rash, chills or faintness. Your team decides what supportive treatment is needed.

first.title: Before leaving
first.text: Write your day-unit and out-of-hours numbers on both cards. Bring them to appointments and urgent assessments. Ask what to do about diarrhoea before taking a medicine to suppress it.

ongoing.title: From cycle 2
ongoing.text: Only durvalumab is scheduled, every 28 days. The immune effects of either medicine may continue after the first visit or after treatment finishes.

ongoing.title: Symptoms at home
ongoing.text: Call promptly about new diarrhoea, cough, breathlessness, jaundice, marked weakness or dizziness. Carry your official immunotherapy alert card and tell the team when you last received treatment.
